name: Familial Adult Myoclonic Epilepsy Type 3
aliases: Adult-Onset Cortical Myoclonus with Epilepsy Type 3

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Proposed Diagnostic Criteria for Familial Adult Myoclonic Epilepsy

criteria.description: Presence of autosomal dominant family history of adult-onset myoclonic epilepsy
Adult-onset cortical myoclonus characterized by stimulus-sensitive, irregular jerks
Occurrence of generalized tonic-clonic seizures in affected individuals
Electroencephalogram (EEG) showing cortical reflex myoclonus with giant somatosensory evoked potentials
Identification of pathogenic pentanucleotide repeat expansions in the SAMD12 gene

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of autosomal dominant family history plus adult-onset cortical myoclonus and generalized tonic-clonic seizures
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic confirmation supports diagnosis but is not mandatory; electrophysiological studies aid in differentiation from other myoclonic epilepsies.

pathognomonic.notes: Characterized by irregular, brief jerks triggered by action or sensory stimuli
Family history consistent with autosomal dominant transmission

imaging: Brain MRI typically normal or nonspecific
No structural abnormalities correlating with symptoms
genetic: Pathogenic pentanucleotide repeat expansions in the SAMD12 gene on chromosome 8q23.3
other: Electroencephalogram (EEG) showing cortical reflex myoclonus with giant somatosensory evoked potentials

distinguishingFeatures: Characteristic 3-6 Hz polyspike and wave EEG pattern
Presence of ataxia and cognitive decline early in disease
Different genetic mutations (e.g., EPM1, CLN genes)

redFlags: Lack of family history in suspected autosomal dominant pattern
references: Ishiura H, et al. Expansions of intronic TTTCA and TTTTA repeats in benign adult familial myoclonic epilepsy. Nat Genet. 2018.
Rufener SL, et al. Familial adult myoclonic epilepsy: clinical and genetic features. Epilepsia. 2020.
Orphanet: Familial Adult Myoclonic Epilepsy Type 3. Orphanet Report Series. 2023.
